'''Andrea Beth Troxel''' is an American biostatistician whose research involves [[longitudinal data]], [[missing data]], the design of [[clinical trial]]s, and [[behavioral economics]] (the study of how financial incentives to medical patients such as [[diet rewards]] can affect their health). She is a professor in the Department of Population Health and director of the Division of Biostatistics in the [[New York University Grossman School of Medicine]].

==Education and career==
Troxel studied applied mathematics at [[Yale University]], graduating [[cum laude]] in 1991. She completed a doctorate (Sc.D.) at the [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]] in 1995.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Methods for the Analysis of Longitudinal Measurements Subject to Nonignorable Non-Monotone Missing Data'', was supervised by David P. Harrington.{{r|harv}} 

After postdoctoral research from 1995 to 1997 at the [[Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center]], she became an assistant professor of clinical public health at [[Columbia University]] in 1997, changing her affiliation to Columbia's Department of Biostatistics in 2000. She moved to the [[Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania]] in 2003, becoming a full professor there in 2011{{r|cv}} before moving to her present position at New York University in 2016.{{r|chibe}} Troxel now co-leads the Zoster Eye Disease Study (ZEDS) as Director and MPI, overseeing the study's Statistics and Data Coordinating Center. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrea Troxel, ScD |url=https://chibe.upenn.edu/expert/andrea-troxelscd/ |access-date=2025-10-20 |website=Center for Health Incentives and Behavioral Economics (CHIBE) |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Troxel was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2012.{{r|fasa}}
